about.title: About
about.author: By {name}
about.tagline: Open-source dive logbook, compatible with Subsurface logbooks.
releaseNotes: Android: screens, the side menu, sheets and dialogs now move with springy motion (a slight bounce where it fits), and the dives of a trip you open slide into place. With “Remove animations” on, none of it moves.

Android: exclusive choices (unit system, dive mode in the filter, Nitrox / Trimix and the fill order in the gas blender) are connected button groups, and every dropdown menu shows a downward chevron instead of a filled triangle.

Android: “Sync now” becomes a split button when synchronisation is manual (the chevron offers to switch to automatic sync or to see the changes not sent yet, which opens the Logbook filtered on the edited dives not sent yet); the Statistics and Tools headers shrink as you scroll, like the Logbook’s.

Android: progress now shows as a wavy line (dive-computer download, offline maps download and update, sign-in), and the circular spinners are replaced by a small shape that morphs while it works (nearby computers, import step, “Connecting…” button). With “Remove animations” on, the wave and the shape stand still.

Android: the actions of a dive (Edit, Share, Plan from this dive, and the ⋮ menu), of a trip (Edit, Add dives, ⋮), of a site (Edit, Open in Maps, ⋮) and of the Logbook’s selection (Create a trip, Export, Delete, ⋮) are in a floating toolbar at the bottom of the screen. A long press on a button shows its name. The bar hides when you scroll down and comes back when you scroll up. The Logbook’s “+” opens the same menu of choices as on tablets, instead of a bottom sheet.
Planner: the Oxygen and Helium menus offer every value by 1 % (oxygen 5 to 100 %, helium 0 to 95 %), and “Other value…” is gone. A mix above 100 % is shown as an error on both fields.

Planner: oxygen, helium, consumption (SAC) and altitude are dropdown menus of the usual values (“Other value…” lets you type another one; the keyboard opens on the same field). A value that is not in the list, such as 33 % read from a dive, shows in the field and heads the menu. A SAC measured on a dive is rounded to 0.01 cu ft/min (0.5 L/min) before it is shown or used.
Planner: “Planner settings” in the ⋮ menu now opens the settings; “Plan from this dive” also works from a dive opened in Statistics or Sites.
Planner, new plan: the “New dive” card shows an empty profile thumbnail (a dashed outline) instead of a “+”, and no longer repeats “No starting dive” on a second line.

Tablets: in the detail pane, the ← back arrow shows only on a screen opened from inside the pane (a dive’s site, a trip’s dive, a statistic’s dive) and goes back one screen in the pane, the list staying as it is; Back does the same, and at the pane’s first screen it leaves the Logbook or returns to it from another section.

Android, download: each dive computer (remembered, nearby or connected) is a card, in two columns on a tablet in landscape; its Bluetooth icon is in tertiary; received dives show the duration above the depth; the failure screen shows a pale red circle with a crossed-out Bluetooth and larger text; on a tablet, the download pane has its ✕ and the floating “+” steps aside while it shows.
Planner: consumption (SAC) has two fields, “At the bottom” and “During deco”. The second one is used for the ascent and the stops; it comes from the planner settings.

Android, tablet: the Logbook's “+” is now the floating button at the bottom right in landscape too (the navigation rail no longer has one), and it opens a menu of three choices above it (download, import a file, log a dive manually) that unfolds over a light veil; the button turns into a ✕, and Back or a tap outside closes the menu. With “Remove animations” on, it appears without motion.
Android, tablet in portrait: no more navigation rail; the ☰ button opens the side menu and the Logbook’s “+” is the floating button again, as on a phone. The rail stays in landscape.
Units: after “Imperial” (or “Metric”) and then a change to a single unit, the other units are kept when the app restarts; before, they went back to metric.
Planner (tablet in portrait): opened beside the tools list, it fits in one column instead of adding one at the right of the screen.
About: the app’s description no longer says “free”.

First launch (Android tablet): in landscape, the title and the dive profile on the left and the three choices on the right; in portrait, the title, the profile across the width, then the choices, centred. No scrolling, even on a small tablet.

Statistics: a total of time under water from 24 h is written in days and hours, without minutes ("80 d 16 h"), in the key figures, the "By …" and "My statistics" rows and the dives of a row; under 24 h it stays in hours and minutes.

Account (iPhone): signing in, creating an account, the confirmation code, bringing your logbook, the import and the git repository take the same layout as on Android: only “Cancel” or “Back” in the bar, a large title, rounded sections, a large capsule button and a dive profile.
Dive profile: the cursor is a plain line in the colour of the curve, without a white outline; the curve buttons (Temperature, ppO₂, Ceiling…) take the colour of their curve when selected.

Sites (tablet): the top of the list takes the band of the other sections, with the "N sites · M dives" summary, the faint profile and the wave; the map stays on the right, up to the top of the screen.
Statistics: the list of dives behind a row opens faster and uses far less memory on a large logbook; only the rows near the screen are drawn.
Dive: when you swipe to the next or previous dive, the site map and the details are already prepared; the screen arrives whole instead of filling in during the slide.

Account (Android): signing in, creating an account, the confirmation code, bringing your logbook and the git repository take the layout of first launch: a large title, the fields in a white card, a large button at the bottom and a dive profile. On a tablet, the title and the card sit side by side in landscape, one above the other in portrait.
Offline maps: they now work on iPhone and iPad too.
Statistics and dive: a value is no longer cut in the middle of a number or a word; when the key figures do not fit side by side, the last one moves whole to the next line.
Taps: a button, a menu or rail entry responds even if the finger slides a little while tapping; before, the tap was sometimes ignored.
Start-up: the app no longer stays on a white screen when it starts before its look has loaded.
Statistics: rows no longer show the maximum depth, and the name of a new statistic comes first.
Dives without a site: each dive shows a thumbnail of its profile and opens its full profile, with the buttons to give it a site.
Site sheet: each dive shows its number.
Statistics: the “By …” sections fold, and are closed at first. The charts and the rows of these sections no longer open anything, and the one-year view is gone.

Sites: the search opens from the magnifier with an animation. The field grows in the top bar, the count of matches sits under it, sites that do not match fade on the map, and the list shows only the results with the match highlighted. The back arrow, the back gesture or the back key closes it and brings the map back to where it was; the cross only clears the text. With reduced motion, the change is a short cross-fade.
Clean up sites: a pencil on each site of a duplicate group opens its editor, then returns to the same place; a group that no longer matches disappears.
Messages: one style for every snackbar, dark on light and light on dark, floating above the bottom of the screen (above the + button when there is one), with one action in blue.
Settings: resetting keeps your list of cylinders.
Clean up sites: "Not duplicates" removes the group from the list and stops suggesting it (on this device); "Undo" puts it back. Renaming or moving one of the two sites makes it suggestible again.
Settings: "Reset all settings" asks for confirmation first, then says "Settings reset". It no longer touches the planner settings.
Logo: the three waves now have shorter gradients, so the layers stay apart at small sizes.
Sites: a menu changes the order of the list (alphabetical or most recent first); a long press selects a site, to merge several sites.
Conflict on several dives: a full-screen dialog with a "Same choice for all" switch and one card per dive, where you touch the version to keep.
Sync conflict: "Later" closes the dialog and leaves you where you were; the Carnet sync status and the side menu sync card reopen it, and it comes back at the next sync attempt.
Offline maps: choosing an area opens on your current position.
Offline maps: an area with no logbook site takes the name of the place.
Offline maps: "Choose on the map" now shows a fixed frame; move and zoom the map under it and the area it covers is what you download. The detail is chosen for you, and the size shown is an estimate.
Offline maps: a search field on "Choose on the map" finds a site of your logbook as you type, or a place when you press search, and moves the map there.

Offline maps: choose an area on the map from Settings to download it (a frame of at most about 3,000 tiles); a space limit and a free-space floor protect the device, and updates are offered with a badge.
Privacy: the policy mentions searching for places on the map.
Offline maps: a search field on "Choose on the map" finds a site of your logbook as you type, or a place when you press search, and puts the rectangle around it.
Offline maps: frame an area on the map from Settings to download it; a space limit and a free-space floor protect the device, and updates are offered with a badge.
Logbook: while scrolling, the current month shows at the top under the bar.
Settings: the water type written on downloaded dives that have none can be chosen (Not specified by default).
Sites: without a network, the map reads the downloaded regions, else a simplified world map; an "Offline" pill says so and a message offers to download the area.
Desaturation: the text under the chart is shorter.
Settings: the app language can be Français (Canada), which says "nuage" and "courriel"; a phone set to French (Canada) picks it by itself.
Dive detail: the cylinder pressure bars run from 0 to the working pressure, with what is left and what was used.
Planner: a plan made from a rebreather dive starts on the diluent, never the oxygen.
Planner: a bar shows the consumed part and the reserve of each gas, another the CNS exposure.
Statistics: charts that do not measure depth (dives per year, durations) are blue.
Editing a rebreather dive: no gas switch depth for the diluent and oxygen, and choosing the use fills in the starting mix (21 % or 100 %).
Sites: the header has the same wave and profile as the other sections, and the map shows under the curve.
Logbook: the sync state (offline with changes waiting, failure, conflict) shows in a pill in the header; a dive waiting to be sent keeps its number and date.
Sync: when it fails while the network works, the Logbook says why (password refused, cloud not answering, git repository refused) and offers what to do.
Planner: the starting dive shows its number and duration, in the planner and in the list to choose it.
Planner settings: no introduction line, the groups follow the title directly.
Planner: “New dive” without the line “Defaults of the Subsurface planner”.
Settings: new group “Default conditions” (water type and altitude), used by the planner and the gas calculator.
Planner redone: planned dives saved in the logbook, several levels and gases, volumes per gas, a decompression model for each plan, sharing a plan.
Edit dive: every cylinder shows all its fields, no collapsed lines.
Share: a PDF icon for the sheet. Export: the first format is named “Logbook file (.ssrf)”.
About: each open source library opens its website in the browser.
Planner: the SAC factor under stress is 2.0 by default.

Settings: default cylinders for open circuit and rebreather (diluent, oxygen, bailout), added when a dive becomes a rebreather dive. Cylinder types: number of dives and a new form. Profile: ceilings reordered, depth grid removed.
Side menu and headers redone: band, account at the top of the menu, centred sync, a summary for each section, logbook search bar. Settings and About use the ☰ menu.
Logbook: rows aligned with the design (no dividers), the dives of an expanded trip in a white surface. Account: same header as the sections.
Logbook: a trip of one dive is shown as a dive, without an arrow.
Logbook: while dragging a dive, a horizontal bar shows where it would be dropped.
Logbook: the dive number is back before the date; an open trip is indented, and its dives can be checked in selection mode.
Logbook: a trip can be selected; “Delete this trip” removes the trip and keeps its dives.
Privacy policy: links and the contact address can be tapped.
Secure connections: the OpenSSL library is replaced by Mbed TLS, compatible with the app’s licence.

Git repository: the logbook can live in your own git repository (GitHub, GitLab, Codeberg or your server) instead of the Subsurface cloud. On the first page, “Use my own git repository”; the access token stays encrypted on the device.
Tablet: the logbook opens the first dive when none is shown.
Sharing: the app no longer stays stuck under a grey veil after sharing a dive or a plan.
Dive profile: the card follows the mock-up (full-width chart, scale down to the maximum depth).
Planner: a saved plan keeps its rates, reserve and other settings, and gives the same result when reopened.
Settings: the units chosen on the device no longer go back to the logbook’s at restart.
Dive detail: the screen follows the mock-up (top bar, trip as a link, sizes and margins, people and tags as chips, a dot on the temperature curve at the cursor).
Dive detail: map of the site behind the header, prepared ahead on Wi-Fi, when the site has GPS coordinates.
Dive detail: a dive on its own no longer shows a trip.
Dive detail: the rating stars stand alone.
Dive detail: “Remove from trip” in the ⋮ menu.
About: the map credit also names OpenFreeMap and OpenMapTiles.
Edit a dive: sections always open, the trip chosen from a list, with a button to remove it.
Edit a dive: choose the main computer when the dive has several.
Settings: Logbook dive computers, to rename, remove or merge duplicates, found by serial number, then by comparing the profiles.
Logbook: “Logbook dive computers” in the ⋮ menu.
New “Trois vagues” logo: app icon, launch screen, menu and About.
Sync conflict: new dialog, readable differences, “Later”, and “Undo” before anything is sent.
Filter (Android): new page, cylinder and gas criteria grouped, a saved filter fills the page, and deleting one offers “Undo”.
Filter: the explanatory sentences under the criteria are gone.
What’s new: the version date next to its number, and the complete list.
Statistics: each row opens the list of its dives.
Logbook: the month shown in the band is more discreet.
Navigation buttons react to a touch at once.
Durations of an hour or more follow the language: “1:11” in English, “1 h 11” in French.
Settings: the “Always in hours and minutes” duration option is gone.
Desaturation: the last logbook dive, and “You can fly” once the wait is over.
Dive rows: the duration above, the depth below.
Settings: the chosen unit system stays after a restart.
First launch (Android): a simpler page, with three buttons and their consequence on one line.
Access token help: one tab per host (GitHub, GitLab, Codeberg).
First launch: full screen on tablets, every choice in view.
Tablet: after signing out, the account’s last dive no longer stays beside the empty logbook.
Tablet: Settings and About open full width, no longer beside the logbook list.
Tablet: section headers get their wavy edge back.

tokenHelp.title: Create an access token
tokenHelp.intro: OpenDives connects to your repository with a personal access token, never with your password. Create a token limited to this one repository, allowed to read and write its contents and nothing else, with an expiry date. The labels below are those of each site’s English interface.
tokenHelp.afterwards: Then paste the token into OpenDives, with your user name. The site shows the token only once: copy it before leaving the page.

github.name: GitHub
github.note: A fine-grained token can be limited to a single repository.
github.s1: Sign in to GitHub, then open Settings (menu of your profile picture).
github.s2: At the bottom of the left column, open Developer settings.
github.s3: Open Personal access tokens, then Fine-grained tokens, then tap Generate new token.
github.s4: Token name: a name you will recognise, for example OpenDives.
github.s5: Expiration: choose a near date, for example in 90 days. On that date the token stops working and you create a new one.
github.s6: Resource owner: your account, or the organisation that owns the repository.
github.s7: Repository access: choose Only select repositories, then the repository of your logbook.
github.s8: Permissions: under Repository permissions, set Contents to Read and write. Add no other permission.
github.s9: Tap Generate token, then copy the token.

gitlab.name: GitLab
gitlab.note: A project access token is limited to one project. On GitLab.com it needs the Premium or Ultimate plan (any licence on a self-managed GitLab server) and the Maintainer or Owner role on the project. Without that, use a personal access token, which reaches all your projects: GitLab cannot limit it to one.
gitlab.p1: Open your project, then in the left sidebar Settings, Access tokens.
gitlab.p3: Token name: a name you will recognise, for example OpenDives.
gitlab.p4: Expiration date: a near date (365 days at most).
gitlab.p5: Role: the lowest one allowed to push to your branch, Developer, or Maintainer if the branch is protected.
gitlab.p7: Tap Create project access token, then copy the token.
gitlab.q1: At the top right, tap your avatar, then Edit profile.
gitlab.q2: In the left sidebar, open Access, then Personal access tokens.
gitlab.q3: In the Generate token list, choose Legacy token.
gitlab.q4: Token name: a name you will recognise. Expiration date: a near date.
gitlab.q6: Tap Generate token, then copy the token.
gitlab.user: In OpenDives, the user name is your GitLab user name. For Git over HTTPS, GitLab accepts any non-empty name with the token.

codeberg.name: Codeberg
codeberg.note: Codeberg’s guide says a token gives full access to your account by default: limit it as below.
codeberg.s1: Sign in to Codeberg, open the menu of your profile picture (Profiles and Settings), then Settings.
codeberg.s3: Under Manage Access Tokens, in Generate New Token, type a Token Name you will recognise, for example OpenDives.
codeberg.s4: If the form offers it, limit the token to your repository: choose Specific repositories, then the repository of your logbook.
codeberg.s5: Permissions: for repository, choose Read and Write. Leave the others on No access.
codeberg.s6: If the form offers an expiry date, choose a near one. Codeberg’s guide does not mention one: without a date, delete the token from this page when you stop using it.
codeberg.s7: Tap Generate Token, then copy the token.
